reason:
The operative contract is problem.txt (no test.py/get_inputs exist): the kernel must evaluate C = A @ dequant(B) with 4-bit packed weights, per-(group,column) scale and zero-point, and it explicitly names AutoGPTQ's quant_matmul_248_kernel as the operation being implemented.

c1 (zero-point off-by-one) is rebutted by t9: with hand-packed 4-bit B the kernel reproduces the (q - (qzeros+1))*scale form to fp32 rounding (max abs 1.35e-6, max rel 3.25e-7) while differing from a bare-qzeros reference by exactly the predicted systematic offset max|A@scale| = 0.71637. The `+1` is the upstream AutoGPTQ packing convention (stored qzeros = true zero-point - 1) for the very kernel problem.txt cites, so `zero[g,n]` in the stated formula is satisfied; this is a representation convention the contract accounts for, not an arithmetic deviation.

c2 (TF32 contamination in tl.dot) is rebutted by t10 and t15: kernel max rel err vs an fp64 reference is 4.69e-7, and across 8 configurations (group sizes 32/64/128, act-order permuted g_idx, M-tail M=33, N-tail N=40, N=96, deep K=512) the worst max rel err is 7.06e-07 with all outputs finite — plain fp32 accumulation accuracy, ~3 orders better than the ~1e-3 TF32 signature the claim predicted. Caveat recorded in evidence: the test GPU is a Tesla T4 (SM75, no TF32 hardware), so the Ampere+ variant of this hypothesis is untestable here; I set it aside because it is a hardware-dependent generalization concern, not a confirmed deviation on the verification environment, and because faithful-fp32 reduction order differences would in any case be within contract.

c3 (unmasked K tail) is confirmed behaviorally: at K=24 the kernel returns non-finite output (max abs err Infinity) while the K=32 control on identical construction is clean (4.02e-7). This is the one unresolved item — its scope stayed `unknown` with empty scope_evidence, because problem.txt states no K divisibility rule and the artifact provides no test.py/get_inputs pinning the tested shapes, while upstream AutoGPTQ is invoked only with group-aligned K (multiples of 128/256 in practice, always multiples of BLOCK_SIZE_K). Under scope policy a confirmed claim with unknown scope and no evidence tying K%16!=0 to the verification domain cannot support reject; "problem.txt does not forbid K=24" is not benchmark coverage. I therefore record it as a real generalization limit (the kernel requires K to be a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16 and silently reads OOB otherwise) rather than a correctness failure against the stated contract.

Net: the behaviors problem.txt explicitly requires — the dequant formula including the named upstream zero-point convention, and faithful evaluation of the matmul in the declared 4-bit format — are confirmed correct across a broad in-domain sweep. Trust, with the K%16!=0 precondition flagged.
